title: Peter Village Enclosure (15Fa166): Early Woodland in Fayette County
summary: Peter Village (15Fa166), an Early Woodland earthwork in Fayette County, has pottery dated to about 409–68 BCE and is a protected site.
bodyMarkdown:
In Fayette County lies Peter Village, an Early Woodland earthwork. Peter Village (site 15Fa166) is one of the enclosures and mounds built by the region's early Woodland peoples. Its builders left no written name for the place.

Pottery from the site is dated to about 409–68 BCE.

Ephraim Squier and Edwin Davis published a plan of Peter Village in their 1848 survey, *Ancient Monuments of the Mississippi Valley*.

Peter Village and other Bluegrass earthworks show that people of the [Adena culture](https://grokipedia.com/page/Adena_culture) and their predecessors shaped the Bluegrass into a landscape of gathering places many centuries before Kentucky's forts and stations. Adena is an archaeologists' name for a shared way of life, not the name of a single tribe.

## Kentucky today

Peter Village is a protected archaeological site, so this site names it but does not map it.
Source: [Adena culture (Grokipedia)](https://grokipedia.com/page/Adena_culture)
